properties.details_shown: Fog, tar, and gulls; the far piers are rotting. Pier four has an upturned skiff where Sela mends her net.

sources.quote: Morning in Gullwick. The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.
There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.

changes.why: Adds the dock details shown this session.

properties.role: Tide-reader and boatwoman; grey braid and salt-stained coat.
properties.played_as: Whispers as if the water might hear; avoids eye contact and watches the tide line; returns to mending her net.

sources.quote: Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.
She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye. She keeps her gaze on the tide line.
Sela, Sella, the dockhands say it both ways.

changes.why: Records the voiced NPC and the GM-confirmed alternate spelling.

sources.quote: There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.

changes.why: Records where the party met Sela.

change.name: Sela's daylight passage to the chapel

properties.what_is_open: Sela has offered to row the party to the old chapel by day only.
properties.next_step: Meet Sela at pier four tomorrow at first light.
properties.deadline: Sela says she will be at pier four tomorrow at first light.

sources.quote: Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
She shrugs and goes back to her net. She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

changes.why: Records the offered passage and rendezvous.

sources.quote: Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.

changes.why: Links the offer to Sela.

sources.quote: You want the old chapel. Everyone who comes here wants the old chapel.
Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.

changes.why: Identifies the destination of Sela's offer.

change.name: Sela's account of the Saltmere flood

properties.statement: Sela says Saltmere flooded forty years ago on the night the bell first rang; her grandmother said the floodwater was warm.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Preserves Sela's historical account and its secondhand detail as claims.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Links the flood account to the existing mine.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, closed for forty years. A black entrance in chalk with a half-rotted timber frame and an overturned rusted cart. Warm air smells of old candle wax. Thirty paces in, warm black water floods the tunnel; wet hymn-book pages float on it and stick to the walls.
properties.state: Closed; the tunnel is flooded thirty paces inside.

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted. A rusted cart lies on its side. The air coming out of it is warm and smells like a church, like old candle wax.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

changes.why: Adds the mine's observed condition and descriptions.

change.name: The hymn page marked M. Brand

properties.statement: A hymn-book page recovered from Saltmere's warm flooded tunnel describes the sea giving back what it takes and bears the pencilled marginal inscription "M. Brand".

sources.quote: About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.
A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

changes.why: Records the inscription without confirming its author.

sources.quote: About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.
A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

changes.why: Records where the page was found.

properties.role: Teo's sister, referred to in play; not encountered this session.

sources.quote: That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: Records the named sister; does not establish the handwriting identification or her presence at Saltmere.

properties.what_changed: A hymn page at Saltmere bears "M. Brand". Teo believes it is Mira's handwriting and that she was there; the GM did not confirm the identification.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".
That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: Advances Teo's goal with a physical clue and his unconfirmed interpretation.

properties.what_is_open: Vessa suspects Maren belongs to a cult and is behind the trouble; Oren suspects she runs the choir. These are player theories, not established facts.

sources.quote: Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this. Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.
You can think that. Roll investigation if you want to search the rest.

changes.why: Keeps the party's suspicions in a thread without changing Maren.

properties.details_shown: Previously described as having sunk into the bay with its bell. At low water the roof, bell tower, and two broken arches stick out of the bay; seaweed hangs from the stones. At midnight pale shapes stand in rows on the submerged chapel floor, like a congregation, and disappear when the bell stops.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches. Seaweed hangs from the stones.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: Adds the chapel's visible ruins and the shapes witnessed this session.

properties.statement: A fisherman says the Kelp Mother pulls children standing too close to the water down by their ankles; the GM identifies this as what fishermen say, not a confirmed creature.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say. They pull their boat up and leave.

changes.why: Preserves local folklore without creating a real NPC.

sources.quote: You get back to Gullwick by dusk, and you decide to go down to the shore below the old chapel ruins anyway, Sela's warning or not.
Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.

changes.why: Records where the warning was given.

sources.quote: (to himself) That's the choir clock at three of six.

changes.why: Advances the existing hidden story clock to the GM's explicit value.

properties.what_is_open: Who or what rings the submerged chapel bell? It rang twelve times again at midnight; the humming grew much louder, and pale shapes stood in rows on the chapel floor before disappearing.

sources.quote: And then, right at midnight, the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times. And the humming is back, but louder. Much louder than two nights ago. You can feel it in your teeth.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: Advances the bell mystery with new observations without identifying the shapes.

sources.quote: Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: Links the observed manifestation to the existing bell thread.

properties.details_shown: A tavern by the docks, with a fire going and the smell of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

changes.why: Records the party's closing location.

properties.role: Innkeeper at the Tarred Gull; huge, with a red beard.
properties.played_as: Laughs at his own jokes and keeps wiping the same mug; teases the party as brave or stupid and offers stew on the house.
properties.knows: Says he has known Maren for thirty years, calls her sharp-tongued with a good heart, and says she lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.
You lot went to the shore at midnight? Brave or stupid. On the house, either way.
Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.
Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Records the voiced innkeeper and attributes his account of Maren to him.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.
The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

changes.why: Records Bram's workplace.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

changes.why: Records where the party last saw Bram.

change.name: Bram's account of Maren's lost brother

properties.statement: Bram says he has known Maren for thirty years and that she lost a brother to the bay; this has not been independently confirmed.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Preserves a new account of Maren's past as an NPC claim.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Links Bram's account to Maren without changing her established properties.

properties.next_step: The party plans to meet Sela at first light tomorrow and dive to the chapel at low tide in daylight.

sources.quote: So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

changes.why: Records the agreed plan without assuming the dive has happened.

properties.next_step: The party has agreed to meet Sela tomorrow at first light for a daylight passage and a low-tide chapel dive.

sources.quote: At low tide, during the day. Not at night, Sela was right about that.

changes.why: Records the party's acceptance of the passage plan.
